results.corrected_extracted: Disposal was observed in 5 studies and self-reported in 3, and was more frequent when results were unexpected: observed disposal at Canadian festivals ranged from 4% (n = 2078, 2015) to 7% (n = 2786, 2014); 10% of young adults in the United States reported disposing of the drug when fentanyl was detected (self-report; n = 81, 2017; the Rhode Island pilot); 0% of people who inject drugs reported doing so in another US study (self-report; n = 125, 2017); in Canadian qualitative work (n = 20), people using opioids were less likely than people using stimulants to intend disposal if fentanyl was found. The review counts the UK festival study of Measham (2019; ref. 32) among the observed-disposal studies and those with more disposal after unexpected results, without giving its rate, and also cites it (n = 230, 2016) for clients' reasons for testing.
